notes.title: Patch Notes for v0.02.02
notes.content:
This update brings the game fully to GameMaker 2.3. This was quite a challenge as a ton of code broke in different places of the game all at once, and figuring out exactly where and why took a lot of time. Now that the full transfer is done I'm not planning on updating to any new engine versions soon, so this should improve update speed.

With this update, the Totem can not be broken anymore by hand. Instead you can now upgrade the totem you start with. This was done in prepartion for full release, where the Totem will play a bigger role. A Totem Destroyer item was added to make sure you can still destroy the Totem if you really want to move to another location.

Besides the Totem, a couple of cool new things where added such as birds, and snow, which I'm really happy with and I hope you guys will enjoy as well.

Lastly, a couple more of the last remaining big bugs have been fixed. The one I have been struggling with ever since starting Nira was the blood particles. It took me a long time to figure out how to make sure they didn't clip through the player, but I finally found a way. This also means the blood splatters on the ground will never despawn (until you walk away far enough for the chunk to unload), which means you can paint the world red!

notes.title: Patch Notes for v0.02.01
notes.content:
This patch contains a ton of bug fixes that were long overdue. The most important bug fix is one that caused boats or tamed animals to disappear over time. I've attempted to fix this bug for about 10 times before, but never managed to find the cause of the issue. This time I found it was directly related to the autosaving feature and decide to rewrite a big part of the saving feature. I've spent a full weekend testing the new saving system and did not encounter a single issue, so I hope it works as it should now! 

The other bugs that were fixed in this patched were caused by the engine upgrade. Moving to GameMaker Studio 2.3 was essential to maintain updates for the coming time, but sadly also caused quite some parts of the code to break. This patch should fix the majority of issues though!

If you find any issues with the current patch, please do report them! There's a button in the menu to report any bugs, and it really helps improve the game.

notes.title: Recap - What Happened In April?
notes.content:
This is a post from my blog. Check out the full post including images and videos on my website: [url=http://baselinegames.com/blog/]http://baselinegames.com/blog/[/url]

April was a special month. A ton of new features and fixes were implemented based on community feedback, a brand new launch trailer was dropped and most importantly; Nira launched in Steam Early Access!

I’m very happy with how the game is performing so far, as the game has a psotivie rating on Steam (80% positive) and I’ve received a ton of positive comments via social media. I’m happy to say it’s definitely performing well enough for me to keep updating Nira for some time to come. So far I’ve pushed a new patch full of community feedback and fixes every single day since launch. I’d like to thank everyone who reported bugs and issues, suggested new features and helped test and improve the game! Thanks to you I can make Nira the best possible version it can be.

This blogpost is dedicated to the changes made with help of the community.

[previewyoutube=JVWm0P6NKik;full][/previewyoutube]

[h3]Hands-Free[/h3]
Right on launch day a first patch was pushed in which the player character no longer needs an item to gather and interact. This is very helpful when in a situation without tools, and also prevents players from accidentally locking themselves up in a home-made prison without any tools to break free.

[h3]Item names[/h3]
Due to the minimalistic look of Nira, it can sometimes be hard to see which items your holding or finding. This becomes increasingly annoying when a totem sends you out on a quest to go find an item of which you have no idea what it looks like. You can now hover your mouse over items in the world or in (chest) inventories to view their names.

Additionally, an item log was introduced showing all items that are gathered or found in the bottom left of the screen. This way you’ll never have to wonder what the pixely circle thingy was that you just picked up!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35949318/861f5746a90af90b330df6b958b2689ae3355f4e.png[/img]

[h3]Map Generator[/h3]
To make the maps a bit more interesting, the map generator was tweaked to form smaller islands with water inbetween. This means resources are a bit more limited too, forcing players to find an explore new islands when you run out of resources.

To make sure exploring doesn’t become a chore, you now start out with a free boat (no problem). The swimming time was also increased and in case you really get yourself stuck on an island with no boat, you can now also ride animals without a saddle (and those good bois swim fast!)

Additionally, you now start out right next to a totem. You can still build totems from the crafting menu and since you only start with a wooden one you’ll definitely have to build better ones along the way. However, this default wooden totem will give a little more objective to new players, hopefully easing them into the game a little smoother.

[url=https://www.instagram.com/p/B_cYxIqH4aR/]Click here to check out some screenshots of what the new map generator produces! [/url]

[h3]Performance[/h3]
Lastly I need to address performance issues. Nira might look simple and minimalistic, but the world is made out of thousands of blocks which are procedurally generated as you walk around. It’s quite a challenge to smoothly load thousands of blocks on screen and save everything off screen at any given time.

Although for most people the game seems to be running smoothly, I am also getting some reports from people experiencing lag. I’ve addressed this on day one, urging people to turn down the graphics settings, and have since then made multiple attempts to improve performance. In a performance patch that was launched a couple of days after release, a crucial memory leak was fixed and general performance was increased. On top of that a new graphics setting was introduced, allowing you to turn off more animations to increase performance. During Early Access I’ll constantly be working on optimizations and new graphical settings to make the game run better.

[h3]To conclude[/h3]
Last month’s goal was to launch Nira, and I think we can safely say that worked out well. I’m very happy with the public reception of the game and it’s definitely performing well enough for me to maintain Nira over the coming time. For next month I would like to set a goal to first fix the major issues people are reporting, and from there work on bigger – more interesting – patches, instead of constant small fixes. I would love to have at least one bigger patch live before next months blog.

And if you have any feedback, make sure to join the Discord and let me know!

[url=https://discord.gg/dJWpEhU][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35949318/bac561a2518fbfc0d6ef915bf8fae1df51d11a30.png[/img][/url]

That’s it for April! Don’t forget to check out Nira on Steam if you haven’t already and if you really don’t want to miss a thing, make sure to follow me on Twitter or Instagram. Thanks for reading, and till next month!
[url=https://twitter.com/BaselineGames_]Twitter[/url] or [url=https://www.instagram.com/baselinegames/]Instagram[/url]. Thanks for reading, and till next month!

notes.title: Recap - What Happened In March?
notes.content:
This is a post from my blog. Check out the full post including images and videos on my website: [url=http://baselinegames.com/blog/]http://baselinegames.com/blog/[/url]

March started off really well with a Beta that was set up together with the lovely folks over at AlphaBetaGamer and iGames, who helped me distribute a great amount of beta keys amongst their audiences. In a week time, over a thousand players entered the wondrous worlds of Nira and I received a ton of very useful feedback. It was also great fun to talk with players through Discord and hear new suggestions for the game. I want to thank everyone who joined the Beta and for the one’s who missed it; don’t worry, there’s only a couple of weeks left before launch!

The main things I took away from the beta was the lack of ‘late’ game content, inventory management, crafting balancing and some interesting bugs and glitches. Goes without saying I made it this months priority to get these things straightened out, which you can read about in this blog post.

[h3]Leveling & Skills[/h3]
To keep long-term players entertained, I’ve added a leveling and skills system. It’s a fairly straight forward system, where you can collect ‘orbs’ by killing creatures. You can choose to invest these orbs in either your character level, or your crafting skills. Your crafting skills allow you to craft higher level recipes in the skill category you train. But skills can only level as high as your character level, so once your skills reach their caps, you’ll have to level up your character level!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35949318/ac966653ba0d9bf0ec50fb7498c50f8deaab5f15.jpg[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35949318/02e83ad71b46b88a64892a08bf299cfa4388b29e.jpg[/img]

[h3]Quests & Merchants[/h3]
But if creatures only appear at night, then how am I gonna get orbs during daytime?

Good question.

I’ve added quests for people to still be able to collect orbs without killing creatures. You can currently get your quests at a totem (which you can build anywhere yourself). Quests require you to collect a certain amount of items and reward you with orbs upon completion.

As some items are pretty rare and hard to come by, I’ve added Merchants. These little guys are walking around the world looking to sell their wares to you. Or… well check out the twitter post below for an alternative way of doing business.

[url=https://twitter.com/BaselineGames_/status/1245415037923180544]View Twitter post here![/url]

[h3]To conclude[/h3]
I’m very happy with this month’s progress. A lot of great new content was added and lots of long overdue bugs were finally fixed. My goal for next month is to stop adding new features, fix all the bugs, add a little more content (like items, sprites, etc.) and most importantly… LAUNCH THE GAME!

That’s it for March! Don’t forget to add Nira to your Steam wishlist if you haven’t already and if you really don’t want to miss a thing, make sure to follow me on [url=https://twitter.com/BaselineGames_]Twitter[/url] or [url=https://www.instagram.com/baselinegames/]Instagram[/url]. Thanks for reading, and till next month!

notes.title: Release Date announcement + New Trailer!
notes.content:
[b]February 20th, 2019[/b] – Today, Baseline Games has revealed the release date for Nira to be April 24th, 2020. A new trailer was published showing a player gradually progress throughout the game. Starting with nothing, a player can explore an endless procedurally generated world looking for resources, which can then be used to craft items and build a base. Players are free to do what they want and can choose to spend their time doing a range of activities like farming, fishing, cooking, taming, riding animals and even flying a plane. But the world of Nira is not without its dangers… During the night, creatures arise, and players will have to carefully prepare by building defenses and weapons to survive.

Nira will release in Early Access on Steam. Through Early Access, Baseline Games hopes to get player feedback, and eventually determine the game’s future together with the community. 

[previewyoutube=wg2atLTNROA;full][/previewyoutube]

About Nira
Nira is a fast-paced survival exploration game. Explore endless procedurally generated worlds to gather resources you need to survive. But when night falls, creatures arise. Build a base, craft weapons and tame wild animals to fight hordes of goblins. Explore, Build, Fight, Survive, and find Nira.

Features
• Explore endless procedurally generated worlds full of resources
• Build a base and craft weapons to defend yourself at night
• Fight off goblins and riddle their ogre leaders with bullets
• Survive nature: catch and cook food, and tame or hunt wild animals

About Baseline Games
Baseline Games is a one-man-studio founded in 2017, currently working on survival exploration game Nira. notes.title: Recap - What Happened In January?
notes.content:
This is a post from my blog. Check out the full post including images and videos on my website: [url=http://baselinegames.com/blog/]http://baselinegames.com/blog/[/url]

The first month of the year is over and it’s been a productive start of the year for Nira. Almost 200 changes were committed since the start of the year, including a ton of new features and content. In this post I’d like to go over a couple of hightlights and give some insight in the plans for next month.

[h3]And there was light![/h3]
The first big thing that was added in January was a lighting system. This was long overdue because the day / night cycle had been in the game for a long time, and finding your way at night had been a real chore. It’s not a very complex lighting system, but it does the job and I think it suits Nira very well. To compliment this I added some torches to finally have some vision during the night. I’m also very happy with how the particle effect came out!

[url=https://twitter.com/BaselineGames_/status/1215966694759378945]Check out the new lighting here![/url]

[h3]Home sweet home[/h3]
Secondly; Beacons! As items and features kept being added, the base building possibilities grew as well. Now as the base building options grew, it also grew more frustrating to lose your base. To solve this issue beacons were added. You put them in the ground and hold the map button to see where they are. You can place up to 4 beacons and change colors to your liking.

[url=https://twitter.com/BaselineGames_/status/1218481422706626560]View the beacons in action here![/url]

[h3]Vertalingen[/h3]
In the first week of the year I asked for help translating Nira. I set up a form with all the localisation lines and asked Twitter to help translate. I was overwhelmed with the amount of responses as I received 25 submissions for over 10 different languages. With the localisation system already in place Nira now supports a total of 20 languages.

[h3]Screens[/h3]
Last but not least, with all the new content added to the game and the new lighting system in place, it felt time to update the screenshots. Check out the Steam store page if you're curious!

[h3]To conclude[/h3]
All and all I’m very happy with the development progress. This post only contains highlights but there’s so much more that was done behind the scenes. I’m happy to say we’re finishing January with a very polished Pre-Alpha version of Nira, and the goal for February is to move on to Alpha. Obviously that’s still a long way from done, but it does mean we’re getting one step closer to Steam Early Access.

That’s it for January! Don’t forget to add Nira to your Steam wishlist if you haven’t already and if you really don’t want to miss a thing, make sure to follow me on [url=https://twitter.com/BaselineGames_]Twitter[/url] or [url=https://www.instagram.com/baselinegames/]Instagram[/url]. Thanks for reading, and till next month!

-Added Player selection at controller connection
-Added controller support for Player 1
-Fixed a bug where Player Dash animation wasn't working properly
-Changed Player walking animation
 
Pre-Alpha v0.00.69          Date: 02-01-2020
-Added Feedback / Bug Report button to main menu ([url=http://baselinegames.com/feedback/]Help improve Nira![/url])
-Added Translation button to main menu ([url=http://baselinegames.com/translate/]Help translate Nira![/url])
-Added sound effect on game start
-Fixed "executable not found" bug at Steam start-up
-Fixed a bug where items with 0 quantity weren't removed from inventory when crafting
-Fixed a bug where starter items would reset back into inventory after loading
-Tweaked menu music to align better with intro
-Changed question mark position in Objectives Menu
-Minor performance tweak to terrainheight calls
-Converted music files to ogg to lower game size
 
Pre-Alpha v0.00.68          Date: 01-01-2020
-Added death sprite for player
-Added black overlay to menus to improve readabilty
-Added "Press F to respawn" message when dead
-Fixed very tiny memory leak in world generator
-Fixed missing text characters (like ëçõ)
-Fixed a bug where removing Soil would crash the game
-Fixed a bug where empty chest would spawn upon dying
-Tweaked world generator to significantly reduce save file size and RAM usage
-Tweaked world generator to generate more varied worlds with less snow
-Tweaked spawn positions to prevent flickering on game start
-Changed font to Noto Sans
-Changed font sizes in crafting GUI and Objectives Overview
-Changed scroll-direction for inventory slots
-Removed unsupported Asian languages
 
Pre-Alpha v0.00.67          Date: 01-01-2020
-Happy New Year!
-Added item / equip names in GUI when holding items
-Fixed a bug where green goblin enemy would flicker while walking
-Fixed a bug where Campfires wouldn't save properly
